## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `temporal-era-segmentation`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-13T17:49:16.342Z.

Planning pass 2026-07-13 (directed maintainer pass): Algorithm (20) temporal non-stationarity mining — change-point era segmentation plus periodicity-aware anticipatory activation. Purpose: the catalog treats decade-deep history as a smooth continuum — log decay (1), age-and-value compaction (15), pm-5qmm age rollups all assume the SAME process generated old and new events. Decades-long workspaces are non-stationary: rewrites, team turnover, process and terminology shifts create ERAS, while stable cadences (release-cut days, month-end, quarterly planning, annual freezes) create CYCLES; optimal context over decades must know which era a precedent came from and which phase of the cycle now is. Cognitive analogs: temporal landmarks / the reminiscence bump (autobiographical memory organizes recall around era boundaries, not uniform time) and circadian/seasonal modulation of memory availability. Part A — online change-point era segmentation: run Bayesian online change-point detection (constant-time per event with standard run-length pruning) over the write-time fold (6) on a handful of population statistics — mutation rate, author-set turnover (sliding Jaccard), vocabulary/embedding-centroid drift, type/status-distribution shift. Detected boundaries partition the timeline into a tiny era table held as fold state (era id, span, signature = top drifted terms + author cohort + dominant components). Consumers: precedent projection (12) discounts cross-era precedents by a per-boundary validity factor and DISCLOSES the gap ("precedent predates era: 2031-storage-rewrite — validity discounted"); contradiction gating (14) takes an era-boundary prior (crossing a boundary lowers the evidence threshold for routing a precedent to verify-before-serve); retrieval alignment: per-era term statistics let the hybrid index expand queries with era-local synonyms mined from boundary-adjacent co-occurrence, so drifted vocabulary still reaches old items. Part B — periodicity-aware anticipatory activation: over folded per-item access streams (ring-buffer binned counts, O(1) update), detect stable cycles via autocorrelation/spectral peaks above a significance floor; items with a confirmed period get a forward-looking activation term anticipated(i,t) = amplitude x kernel(phase distance of t to next predicted peak), added as one more explainable linear signal (3) — release-tooling items warm up BEFORE the cut. Strictly additive: (1) stays the backward-looking base, (20B) is the disclosed forecast term. Spectrum behavior: small/young workspaces — no boundary accumulates enough evidence and no cycle passes the floor, both parts emit nothing, zero behavior change; decades-deep archives — era table stays dozens-of-rows small, periodicity state is O(items with recurring access), everything folds at write time (no daemon, ADR pm-i7i4). Distinct from (1) (smooth stationary decay — this adds the structure decay cannot see), from (15)/pm-5qmm (compress by AGE/value — this segments by REGIME; an era boundary is not an age), from (14) alone (pairwise per-precedent evidence; 20A is a population-level prior over ALL cross-era retrieval), from pm-vvib candidate 9 encoding specificity (per-item write-time situation stamps; this is corpus-level temporal structure), and from (16) (relational geography, not time). Ownership: era/periodicity fold state = pm-3hps (wave 3); era-conditioned discounting + query expansion = wave-4 mined territory alongside (12); envelope disclosure follows the (18)/(19) pattern.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
